title: Rabbit Lands inventory, item inspection and preview — five compact concepts
intended_camera: Flat front-facing desktop game UI screenshot
purpose: Compare compact layouts and information hierarchy for inventory, full item inspection and the selected-item text preview.
implementation_note: These are generated visual explorations. Pixel coordinates, slot counts, wording and gameplay actions remain implementation decisions; none of these images changes the runtime UI.

concepts.title: 01 · Unified compact
concepts.description: One compact inventory window; item preview expands into full inspection in the same panel.

review.reason: Useful compact exploration with clear shared preview/inspection; the generated grid shows 30 cells despite the intended 36. Slot geometry must be resolved in implementation.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity Rabbit Lands inventory / item-inspection UI exploration, one landscape image per concept.
Reference image 1 is the current inventory with a short text preview; reference image 2 is the current oversized inspection popup. They establish actual functionality and the problems to fix, not layouts to reproduce. Reference image 3 is a Rabbit Lands HUD style exploration; use its refined classic dark-brown/charcoal panels, warm restrained brass trim, cream typography, and chunky hand-painted fantasy item icon language. This is an EXPLORATION, not an approved implementation.
Primary goal: substantially reduce screen obstruction, improve information hierarchy, legibility and usability for the inventory, the selected-item text preview below it, and full item inspection. Preserve visibility of the world and player. No giant center modal. No ornate bulky frames. Do not shrink type to make the UI compact. Merge redundant controls, use progressive disclosure, and keep action targets comfortable for desktop mouse use.
Presentation: polished 1920x1080 widescreen game UI design image, flat front-facing screen capture, no physical monitor. An understated stylized Eloria stone courtyard / green landscape behind it, center player unobscured. Around 70% of the game view remains clear. Render focused inventory UI only; do not copy all the unrelated party/chat HUD in reference 3. Put a small elegant concept title at top left. No explanatory paragraph, no dimension claims, no marketing copy. Crisp readable text, carefully aligned components. A faint player resource bar along the very bottom is fine.
Content: backpack has 36 slots in total, plus 8 worn-equipment slots. Show realistic painted icons (bread, red potion, sword, boots, ore, herbs, leather, wood), a clearly outlined selected slot, easy-to-scan quantities, and some empty slots. Counts use concise formatting in cells, exact amounts in inspection. Selected example is Hearth Bread, category Food, stack 24, effects '+40 Food', 'Weight 2', description 'Baked before dawn at the Four Gates ovens.' Load '205 / 320'. Keep preview below the pack legible, at most two lines when collapsed. Explicit inspection must be visibly supported and coherent with that preview. Primary action Use or Equip follows item type; contextual secondary actions include Inspect, Split, Drop. Bulk actions and Protection belong under a compact More menu. Quantity controls use a small 'Qty' field with 1, 5, 10, All presets, not a wide extra control row. Surface only relevant actions. A short 'Esc Close' hint is fine.
Visual constraints: professional shippable fantasy MMORPG interface, coherent warm hand-painted matte materials, strong value contrast, quiet background, thin trim, restrained accents. Avoid excessive leather/paper/wood texture, tiny crowded text, glows, huge decorative item art, extensive labels, unnecessary new systems, extra item rarity or statistics not in this brief. All visible UI panels must fit fully on-screen. 
CONCEPT 01 — UNIFIED COMPACT WINDOW.
Small single floating inventory toward the right side; the entire expanded module occupies roughly 26% of screen width and 50% of height. Shared header Inventory, search icon, More, close. Two-column body: narrow equipment rail with eight worn slots on the left; compact six-by-six backpack grid on the right. No vertical bulk-action button stack. Below the body, a short selected-item strip displays a bread thumbnail, Hearth Bread, Food, x24 and '+40 Food · Weight 2'. This preview expands downward INSIDE THE SAME WINDOW for Inspect. Show it expanded here: concise description and Use / Split / Drop action row with Qty. A subtle chevron collapses this description to the two-line preview. Load in a thin footer. The item name should appear only once within the component; preview and inspection are one component, not duplicate content. The expanded inspector should add only enough height for its actual content. Preserve all 36 backpack slots and 8 equipment slots visible at once. Best balance of familiar layout and compactness.
prompts.reason: Initial exploration used too much screen space; revised to a smaller desktop scale.
